rules.title: State the claim, do not frame it
rules.text: A claim stated as a contrast — 'not just a score, but a judgment', 'a stage, not an assistant' — spends a line on framing and adds nothing the plain statement does not have. The contrast is the reader's to draw.

inspection.pattern: (?i)\bnot just\b|\bisn'?t just\b|\bnot merely\b|\bmore than just\b|\bnot only\b.{0,60}\bbut\b

judgement.question: Is this sentence framing its claim as a contrast rather than stating it — would the same sentence carry the same information without the 'not just X' construction?

criteria.true: the contrast is rhetorical: the sentence says everything it has to say without it, and the framing is there for emphasis
criteria.false: the contrast carries information — two things that differ in a way the document has measured or defined — or it is inside a quotation
